definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Having gone beyond the three guṇas, from which the body arises, the embodied one, freed from birth, death, old age and pain, attains immortality (14.20). Asked for the marks, the conduct and the means (14.21), Kṛṣṇa describes one who neither hates illumination, activity and delusion when present nor longs for them when gone; who sits as one indifferent, unshaken, knowing that it is the guṇas that act; who is the same in pain and pleasure, toward clod, stone and gold, in blame and praise, honour and dishonour, toward friend and foe, and has given up all undertakings (14.22-14.25). The means named is serving the Lord with unswerving bhakti-yoga, by which one goes beyond the guṇas and becomes fit for becoming brahman (14.26); seeing no doer but the guṇas and knowing what is beyond them leads to the Lord's state (14.19).

relations.note: the state of one no longer bound by the guṇas (14.5, 14.20)

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The living being as the Lord's eternal portion (aṃśa)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: An eternal portion (aṃśa) of the Lord alone, having become the living being in the world of the living, draws to itself the senses with the mind as sixth, which abide in prakṛti (15.7). As master (īśvara) of the body it takes them with it when it obtains a body and when it departs, as the wind carries scents from their source (15.8); presiding over hearing, sight, touch, taste, smell and the mind it partakes of objects (15.9). The deluded do not see it departing, staying or enjoying, accompanied by the guṇas; those with the eye of knowledge, and yogins who strive, see it abiding in themselves (15.10-15.11). The commentators divide on the sense of 'portion'.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Great brahman as the Lord's womb; the Lord as seed-giving father (BhG 14.3–4)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The Lord's womb is great brahman (mahad brahma); in it he places the germ, and from that the origin of all beings comes (14.3). Of whatever forms come into being in all wombs, great brahman is the womb and the Lord is the seed-giving father (14.4). The commentators take 'great brahman' here as prakṛti; the verses call it only 'great brahman' and 'my womb'.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The guṇa prevailing at death and the next birth (BhG 14.14–18)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The guṇa prevailing at death decides what follows: dying when sattva has increased, the embodied one reaches the stainless worlds of those who know the highest (14.14); dying in rajas it is born among those attached to action, and dying in tamas in deluded wombs (14.15). Those abiding in sattva go upward, the rājasa stay in the middle, the tāmasa go downward (14.18). The fruit of well-done action is sāttvika and stainless, of rajas pain, of tamas ignorance (14.16).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The field and the knower of the field (kṣetra–kṣetrajña)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: This body is called the field and whoever knows it the knower of the field (13.2); the Lord is to be known as the knower of the field in all fields, and knowledge of field and knower is knowledge (13.3). The field in brief: the great elements, the sense of 'I', understanding, the unmanifest, the ten faculties and the one, the five domains of the senses, desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, sentience and steadiness, with their modifications (13.6-13.7). Every being arises from the union of field and knower (13.27); the possessor of the field illumines the whole field as the sun the world (13.34); those who know their difference with the eye of knowledge go to the highest (13.35).

members: ekam ('the one'; manas per the commentators)

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Absence of pride and pretence, non-harming, forbearance, uprightness, attendance on the teacher, purity, steadiness, restraint of oneself; dispassion toward sense-objects, absence of the sense of 'I', keeping in view the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain; non-attachment, not clinging to son, wife and home, constant evenness of thought amid the desired and undesired; unswerving devotion to the Lord through a yoga with no other; resort to secluded places, no delight in crowds; constancy in knowledge of adhyātma, and keeping in view the aim of the knowledge of reality — this is called knowledge; what is otherwise is ignorance (13.8-13.12; 13.7-11 in the 700-verse numbering).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sattva, rajas and tamas, born of prakṛti, bind the imperishable embodied one in the body (14.5): sattva, stainless and illuminating, by attachment to happiness and knowledge; rajas, of the nature of passion, by attachment to action; tamas, born of ignorance, by heedlessness, indolence and sleep (14.6-14.9). Each prevails by overpowering the other two (14.10); their signs are light and knowledge; greed, activity, undertakings, restlessness and longing; absence of light, inactivity, heedlessness and delusion (14.11-14.13); they decide the destiny at death and have their fruits (14.14-14.18). They are born of prakṛti with the modifications (13.20); attachment to them causes births (13.22); they nourish the branches of the aśvattha (15.2).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The guṇas as the doers of action

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The seer who sees no doer other than the guṇas and knows what is beyond them attains the Lord's state (14.19); the one beyond the guṇas stands firm, knowing 'it is the guṇas that act' (14.23). Actions are done by prakṛti alone (13.30).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The self is not the agent; the guṇas act

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Prakṛti is the cause in agency, puruṣa in experiencing (13.21); whoever sees actions done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer sees truly (13.30); the beginningless supreme self, being without guṇas, neither acts nor is stained though in the body (13.32), as space is not stained (13.33).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The inverted aśvattha tree of saṃsāra

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: They speak of an imperishable aśvattha with roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the metres; who knows it knows the Veda (15.1). Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the guṇas, with sense-objects as shoots; its roots stretch below in the human world, binding through action (15.2). Its form, end, beginning and foundation are not perceived here; it is to be cut with the strong weapon of non-attachment, and the place of no return sought (15.3-15.4). The chapter does not itself name the tree saṃsāra.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The perishable, the imperishable and the highest person

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: There are two persons in the world, the perishable — all beings — and the imperishable, called the one standing firm (kūṭastha) (15.16); the highest person is another, called the supreme self, the imperishable lord who enters and sustains the three worlds (15.17); since the Lord is beyond the perishable and higher than the imperishable he is celebrated as puruṣottama (15.18); whoever knows him thus worships him with his whole being (15.19). The commentators divide on what the imperishable is.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The imperishable person (akṣara puruṣa), called kūṭastha, set beside the perishable, which is all beings; the highest person, the Lord, is higher even than it (15.16-15.18).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Prakṛti and puruṣa are both beginningless; the modifications and the guṇas arise from prakṛti (13.20); it is the cause in agency concerning effect and cause (13.21); puruṣa abides in it and experiences the guṇas born of it (13.22); all actions are done by prakṛti alone (13.30); the three guṇas are born of it (14.5); the senses and mind abide in it (15.7).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Beginningless like prakṛti (13.20), puruṣa is the cause in experiencing pleasure and pain (13.21); abiding in prakṛti it experiences the guṇas, and attachment to them is the cause of its births in good and bad wombs (13.22). The highest person in this body is onlooker, consenter, sustainer, experiencer, great lord, and is called the supreme self (13.23); whoever knows puruṣa and prakṛti with the guṇas thus is not born again (13.24). Chapter 15 speaks of two persons, perishable and imperishable, and the highest person beyond both (15.16-15.18).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The knowable is the beginningless highest brahman, knowing which one attains immortality; it is called neither being nor non-being (13.13); it has hands, feet, eyes, heads and ears everywhere and stands enveloping all (13.14); it appears through the qualities of the senses yet is devoid of them, is without guṇas yet their experiencer (13.15); it is outside and inside beings, far and near, not to be discerned because of its subtlety (13.16); undivided yet as if divided, it sustains, devours and brings forth beings (13.17); it is the light of lights, beyond darkness, seated in the heart of all (13.18). Seeing the manifold resting in the one, one reaches brahman (13.31). 'Great brahman' is the Lord's womb (14.3-14.4); the Lord is the foundation of brahman (14.27).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The Lord in the heart of all beings

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The knowable is seated in the heart of all (13.18); the supreme lord abides equally in all beings, not perishing when they perish (13.28-13.29); the Lord is seated in the heart of all, and from him come memory, knowledge and their loss (15.15).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Attachment to the guṇas is the cause of puruṣa's births in good and bad wombs (13.22); the guṇa prevailing at death decides the next birth (14.14-14.15, 14.18); the Lord's portion, as master of the body, takes the senses and mind with it when it obtains a body and when it leaves one, as the wind carries scents (15.8). Whoever knows puruṣa and prakṛti is not born again (13.24).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Chapters 13-15 name the goal as: not being born again (13.24); crossing beyond death (13.26); going to the highest goal (13.29) or the highest (13.35); reaching brahman (13.31); the Lord's state (13.19, 14.19); the highest perfection, and sameness of nature with the Lord, not born at creation nor troubled at dissolution (14.1-14.2); immortality (13.13, 14.20); fitness for becoming brahman (14.26); the place, the Lord's supreme abode, from which none return (15.4-15.6); release from the prakṛti of beings (13.35).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The conjunction of puruṣa and prakṛti (saṃyoga)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Whatever being is born, stationary or moving, arises from the union (saṃyoga) of the field and the knower of the field (13.27); puruṣa, abiding in prakṛti, experiences the guṇas born of it (13.22). The text's own phrase is kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyoga.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The paths of the Gītā: action, knowledge, meditation and devotion

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Some see the self in themselves by themselves through meditation, others by the yoga of sāṃkhya, others by the yoga of action (13.25); others, not knowing thus, worship after hearing from others and they too cross death (13.26); unswerving bhakti-yoga carries one beyond the guṇas (14.26). The verses set these side by side without ranking them.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Teacher, transmission and secrecy in the Gītā and epic

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The field and its knower have been sung by the seers in many ways, in the metres, and in the words of the brahma-sūtras (13.5); the teaching of the highest person is called the most secret teaching, understanding which one is wise and has done what is to be done (15.20); attendance on the teacher is among the items called knowledge (13.8).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Having cut the aśvattha with non-attachment, one seeks the place of no return with the words 'I take refuge in that very primal person from whom the ancient stream of activity flowed forth' (15.4).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The field is listed as the great elements, the sense of 'I', understanding, the unmanifest, the ten faculties and the one, and the five domains of the senses (13.6) — twenty-four items, though the verse gives no number — to which desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, sentience and steadiness are added (13.7).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The highest brahman, the knowable, is said to be neither being (sat) nor non-being (asat) (13.13).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Unswerving devotion to the Lord through a yoga with no other is counted among the items called knowledge (13.11); the Lord's devotee who understands field, knowledge and knowable comes to his state (13.19); serving him with unswerving bhakti-yoga one goes beyond the guṇas (14.26); whoever knows him as the highest person worships him with his whole being (15.19).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Some see the self in themselves by themselves through meditation (13.25); seeing the lord equally everywhere one does not harm oneself by oneself (13.29); whoever sees oneself as not the doer sees truly (13.30); the supreme self neither acts nor is stained though in the body (13.32), and the self present in the body is unstained like space (13.33); striving yogins see the one abiding in themselves (15.11).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Constant evenness of thought amid the desired and undesired is among the items called knowledge (13.10); the one beyond the guṇas is the same in pain and pleasure, toward clod, stone and gold, the pleasant and unpleasant, blame and praise, honour and dishonour, friend and foe (14.24-14.25).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The Lord's eternal portion 'having become the living being' (jīva-bhūta) in the world of the living draws the senses and mind (15.7), carries them from body to body (15.8) and partakes of objects (15.9).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The self common to all men (vaiśvānara)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The Lord, having become vaiśvānara and dwelling in the bodies of breathing beings, joined with prāṇa and apāna, digests the fourfold food (15.14).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: The body as the city of nine gates (navadvāra pura)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: When the light of knowledge arises in all the gates of this body, sattva has increased (14.11).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The roots of the aśvattha stretch below in the human world, binding through action (karma-anubandhin) (15.2); rajas binds the embodied one by attachment to action (14.7).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.
